'''Jonas Kubilius''' (27 July 1921 – 30 October 2011) was a Lithuanian [[mathematician]] who worked in [[probability theory]] and [[number theory]]. He was [[rector (academia)|rector]] of [[Vilnius University]] for 32 years, and served one term in the [[Seimas|Lithuanian parliament]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lrytas.lt/-13200014521318305746-ilgaam%C5%BEi%C5%A1kumo-lygt%C4%AF-i%C5%A1sprend%C4%99s-j-kubilius-per-gyvenim%C4%85-%C4%97jo-nedejuodamas-d%C4%97l-smulkmen%C5%B3.htm|title=Ilgaamžiškumo lygtį išsprendęs J.Kubilius per gyvenimą ėjo nedejuodamas dėl smulkmenų|last=Jonušienė|first=Danutė|date=2011-10-30|publisher=[[Lietuvos rytas]]|language=lt|access-date=1 November 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111031233927/http://www.lrytas.lt/-13200014521318305746-ilgaam%C5%BEi%C5%A1kumo-lygt%C4%AF-i%C5%A1sprend%C4%99s-j-kubilius-per-gyvenim%C4%85-%C4%97jo-nedejuodamas-d%C4%97l-smulkmen%C5%B3.htm|archive-date=31 October 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.delfi.lt/news/daily/lithuania/mire-buves-vu-rektorius-profjkubilius.d?id=51256469|title=Mirė buvęs VU rektorius prof.J.Kubilius|author=(from [[ELTA]] and [[Baltic News Service]])|date=2011-10-30|publisher=[[Delfi (web portal)|DELFI]]|language=lt|access-date=1 November 2011}}</ref>

==Life and education==
Kubilius was born in Fermos village, Eržvilkas county, [[Jurbarkas District Municipality]], [[Lithuania]] on 27 July 1921. He graduated from Raseiniai high school in 1940 and entered [[Vilnius University]], from which he graduated ''[[summa cum laude]]'' in 1946 after taking off a year to teach mathematics in middle school.<ref name="Masaitis">{{cite journal |last=Masaitis |first=Česlovas |year=1992 |title=An Ordinary Birthday of an Extraordinary Person |journal=Lituanus |volume=32 |issue=2 |pages=31–40 |issn=0024-5089 |url=http://www.lituanus.org/1992_2/92_2_03.htm |access-date=2009-04-18 |archive-date=2019-08-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190804194053/http://www.lituanus.org/1992_2/92_2_03.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Kubilius received the [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree in 1951 from [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad University]].<ref name="significant dates">{{cite web | title=Prof. Dr. Habil. Jonas KUBILIUS: Significant dates | url=http://www.mii.lt/index.php?siteaction=personnel.view&id=422&menu=biography&lang=en | publisher= Institute of Mathematics and Informatics | date=2007-02-12 | access-date=2009-04-16}}</ref> His thesis, written under [[Yuri Linnik]], was titled ''Geometry of Prime Numbers''.<ref name="Masaitis" /><ref name="Forty Years History">{{cite journal |last=Rutkauskas |first=Stasys|year=1996 |title=Forty Years History of the Institute of Mathematics and Informatics |journal=Annual Report |pages=5–10 |url= http://www.mii.lt/files/09_an_mii_40_rutk_96.pdf |publisher=Institute of Mathematics and Informatics| access-date=2009-04-16 }}</ref> He received the [[Doctor of Sciences]] degree ([[habilitation]]) in 1957 from the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in [[Moscow]].<ref name="significant dates" /><ref name="Forty Years History" />

==Career==
Kubilius had simultaneous careers at [[Vilnius University]] and at the [[Lithuanian Academy of Sciences]]. He continued working at the university after receiving his bachelor's degree in 1946, and worked as a lecturer and assistant professor after receiving his [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate]] degree in 1951. In 1958 he was promoted to professor and was elected [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the university. He retired from the rector's position in 1991 after serving almost 33 years, and remained a professor in the university.<ref name="Masaitis" />

During the [[Khrushchev Thaw]] in the middle 1950s there were attempts to make the university "Lithuanian" by encouraging the use of the [[Lithuanian language]] in place of [[Russian language|Russian]] and to revive the Department of Lithuanian Literature. This work was started by the rector [[Juozas Bulavas]], but [[Stalinism|Stalinists]] objected and Bulavas was dismissed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vilnius University 1579–2004 |url=http://www.vu.lt/site_files/InfS/Leidiniai/Vilnius_University_1579_2004.pdf |publisher=Vilnius University |access-date=2009-04-17 }}</ref>{{Rp|50–51}} Kubilius replaced him as rector and was more successful in resisting pressure to [[Russification|Russify]] the University: he returned Lithuanian language and culture to the forefront of the University.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Clark |first1=Terry D. |editor1-first=Richard |editor1-last=Frucht |title=Eastern Europe: an introduction to the people, lands, and culture |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lVBB1a0rC70C |access-date=2009-04-17|volume=1 |year=2005 |publisher=ABC-CLIO |isbn=978-1-57607-800-6 |pages=165–201 |chapter=Lithuania }}</ref>{{Rp|190}} Česlovas Masaitis attributes Kubilius's success to "his ability to manipulate within the complex bureaucratic system of the Soviet Union and mainly because of his international recognition due to his scientific achievements."<ref name="Masaitis" /> Kubilius also encouraged the faculty to write research papers in Lithuanian, English, German, and French, as well as in Russian, and he himself wrote several textbooks in Lithuanian.<ref name="Masaitis" /> Jonas Kubilius known by pseudonym Bernotas was also involved in [[Lithuanian partisans|Lithuanian partisan]] movement.<ref>{{cite web |title=Didžiosios Kovos partizanų apygarda |url=http://genocid.lt/Leidyba/4/kronika3.htm |language=lt |access-date=18 April 2018 }}</ref> According to some sources Lithuanian partisans suggested him to continue studies and stay alive to work for Lithuania in the future.

In 1952 Kubilius became an employee of the [[Lithuanian Academy of Sciences]] in the Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy Sector. He initially promoted the development of [[probability theory]] in Lithuania, and later the development of [[Differential equation|differential equations]] and [[mathematical logic]]. In 1956 the Physical and Technical Institute was reorganized and Kubilius became head of the new Mathematical Sector.<ref name="Forty Years History" /> When he became rector of Vilnius University in 1958 he gave up his duties as head and was succeeded by [[Vytautas Statulevičius]] in 1960.<ref>{{cite web | title=History of the Institute of Mathematics and Informatics: dates, facts, people, and comments; Institute of Physics and Mathematics (IPhM) before the first reorganization (1956-1966) | url=http://www.mii.lt/index.php?siteaction=pages.browse&page=phmi1 | publisher=Institute of Mathematics and Informatics | access-date=2009-04-16}}</ref> In 1962 he was elected a member of the Academy.<ref name="Masaitis" /> He held a position as Principal Scientific Worker at the Institute of Mathematics and Informatics,<ref>{{cite web | title=Prof. Dr. Habil. Jonas KUBILIUS | url=http://www.mii.lt/index.php?siteaction=personnel.view&id=422&lang=en | publisher=Institute of Mathematics and Informatics | date=2007-02-12 | access-date=2009-04-16}}</ref> which split from the Lithuanian Academy of Sciences and is now an independent state scientific institute.<ref>{{cite web | title=Institute of Mathematics and Informatics | url=http://www.mii.lt/files/imi_en.ppt | format = PPT | publisher=Institute of Mathematics and Informatics | date=April 3, 2005 | access-date=2009-04-16}}</ref>

Kubilius's scientific work was in the areas of [[number theory]] and [[probability theory]].<ref name="Masaitis" /> The [[Turán–Kubilius inequality]]<ref name="Tenenbaum">{{cite book | title=Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory | last=Tenenbaum | first=Gérald | series=Cambridge studies in advanced mathematics | volume=46 | publisher=Cambridge University Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gX_WAQm7dwoC | year=1995 | isbn=0-521-41261-7 }}</ref>{{Rp|316}} and the [[Kubilius model]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ford |first1=Kevin |editor1-last=Charpentier |editor1-first=Éric |editor2-last=Lesne |editor2-first=Annick |editor3-last=Nikolʹskiĭ |editor3-first=Nikolaĭ Kapitonovich |title=Kolmogorov's Heritage in Mathematics |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SpTv44Ia-J0C |access-date=2009-04-17 |year=2007 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-540-36349-1 |pages=97–108 |chapter=From Kolmogorov's theorem on empirical distribution to number theory}}</ref>{{Rp|104}} in [[probabilistic number theory]] are named after him. Eugenijus Manstavičius and Fritz Schweiger wrote about Kubilius's work in 1992, "the most impressive work has been done on the statistical theory of arithmetic functions which almost created a new research area called Probabilistic Number Theory. A monograph devoted to this topic was translated into English in 1964 and became very influential."<ref>{{cite book |editor1-first=Eugenijus |editor1-last=Manstavičius |editor2-first=Fritz |editor2-last= Schweiger |title=Analytic and probabilistic methods in number theory |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PewI8EsBTWEC |access-date=2009-04-17 |series=New Trends in Probability and Statistics |volume=2 |year=1992 |publisher=VSP |location=Utrecht |isbn=978-90-6764-094-7 |first1=Eugenijus |last1=Manstavičius |first2=Fritz |last2= Schweiger |chapter=Preface |page=xi }}</ref> (The monograph is ''Probabilistic Methods in the Theory of Numbers.'')

Kubilius organized the first [[List of mathematics competitions|mathematical olympiad]] in Lithuania in 1951,<ref>{{cite web |first=Eugenijus |last=Stankus |author2=Romualdas Kašuba |title=Some Additional Mathematical Activities in Mathematical Education in Lithuania |url=http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/icmis16plitkasuba.pdf |date=2006-04-19 |access-date=2009-04-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091013220444/http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/icmis16plitkasuba.pdf |archive-date=2009-10-13 }}</ref> and he wrote books of problems for students to use in preparing for the olympiads.<ref name="Masaitis" /> He was a past president of the [[Lithuanian Mathematical Society]].<ref name="Masaitis" />

In addition to his scientific and administrative work, Kubilius was a member of the [[Seimas]] (Lithuanian parliament) from 1992 to 1996.<ref>{{cite web | title=Lieutvos Respubliko Seimas - Jonas KUBILIUS, Member of the Seimas 1992–1996 | url=http://www3.lrs.lt/docs3/kad2/w5_lrs.seimo_narys-p_asm_id=122&p_kalb_id=2&p_kade_id=2.htm | publisher=Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania | date=August 18, 2006 | access-date=2009-04-16}}</ref>
